name: Dialog::event
prose: Precondition: event is a non-null pointer to a valid QEvent and the Dialog's d-pointer is valid. Postcondition: the function has these exits. (1) Expose: if the platform is not Wayland, or the process is KWin, or isExposed() is false, it returns QQuickWindow::event(event) at once. If Wayland outside KWin, exposed, d->needsSetupNextExpose is true and isVisible() is true, it calls d->updateVisibility(true), calls QQuickWindow::event(event) and keeps the result, calls d->updateTheme(), sets d->needsSetupNextExpose to false and returns the kept result. Any other Expose (Wayland outside KWin, exposed, but needsSetupNextExpose false or not visible) falls through to the forwarding block below. (2) Show calls d->updateVisibility(true); Hide calls d->updateVisibility(false) and sets d->needsSetupNextExpose to true; Move with d->type != Dialog::OnScreenDisplay calls PlasmaShellWaylandIntegration::get(this)->setPosition(me->pos()); each of these then falls through. (3) Forwarding block, entered only when d->mainItem is non-null and its size is not empty: for MouseMove/MouseButtonPress/MouseButtonRelease, when d->resizableEdges is non-zero, a MouseMove for which d->updateMouseCursor(globalPosition) returns true returns QQuickWindow::event(event), and a MouseButtonPress whose d->hitTest(globalPosition) & d->resizableEdges is non-zero calls startSystemResize(sides) and returns true; otherwise, if geometry() contains the global position and the main item does not contain the scene position, it builds an adjusted QMouseEvent, sends it to this window only if isVisible(), and returns true whether or not it was sent. Wheel, DragEnter, DragMove and Drop events whose position is outside the main item likewise build an adjusted copy, send it only if isVisible(), and return true (no geometry() check for these). Events inside the main item, DragLeave and all other event types leave the block via break/default. (4) Every path not returned above ends with return QQuickWindow::event(event). The event is not owned or deleted by this function; the adjusted copies are stack objects.
note: slice shows only the body; checked against dialog.cpp:1370-1527. Reviewers' points (Move sets Wayland position; mouse forwarding needs geometry containment and visibility) were right about the old prose and are now stated (1394-1404, 1431-1444). Old prose omitted that the forwarding block needs a non-empty mainItem (1409) and that an Expose with needsSetupNextExpose false or invisible falls through (1387-1393).

name: DrmOutput::computeCapabilities
prose: Precondition: m_connector and m_gpu are valid; the function is const and reads m_connector properties, m_gpu queries, m_autoRotateAvailable, m_autoBrightnessAvailable and m_state (highDynamicRange, brightnessDevice, allowSdrSoftwareBrightness, detectedDdcCi) as currently stored. It is called from the DrmOutput constructor (drm_output.cpp:64) as well as later (e.g. lines 278, 612, 794, 812), so it must not assume the construction is finished; during the constructor call those members hold their initial values. Postcondition: returns a Capabilities set that contains Dpms, IccProfile and CustomModes and additionally: Overscan if overscan or underscan is valid; Vrr if vrrCapable is valid and true; Tearing if the gpu supports async pageflips; RgbRange if broadcastRGB is valid; WideColorGamut if colorspace is valid and has a BT2020_RGB or BT2020_YCC enum, the EDID supports BT2020, and the gpu check passes (on i915: s_allowColorspaceIntel override set or kernel version at least 6.11; on NVIDIA: s_allowColorspaceNVidia override set or driver version at least 565.57.1; on any other gpu: no extra condition); HighDynamicRange if hdrMetadata is valid, the EDID supports PQ and WideColorGamut was just added; AutoRotation if the connector is internal and m_autoRotateAvailable; BrightnessControl if m_state.highDynamicRange, m_state.brightnessDevice or m_state.allowSdrSoftwareBrightness; AutomaticBrightness only when BrightnessControl was added, m_autoBrightnessAvailable is true and it is not the case that HDR is off with a brightness device that uses DDC/CI; BuiltInColorProfile if the EDID is valid and has a default colorimetry; DdcCi if m_state.detectedDdcCi; MaxBitsPerColor if maxBpc is valid; Edr if m_state.brightnessDevice is set and the output is internal; SharpnessControl if the gpu supports sharpness. No locks are taken and nothing is allocated or handed to the caller besides the returned value.
note: slice cut includes the constructor. Reviewer (round 15) is right: 'fully constructed' is false since drm_output.cpp:64 calls it inside the constructor initializer of setInformation; precondition rewritten. Old prose otherwise matched lines 213-270.

No Wayland call is made by the constructor itself.

name: WaylandQPainterCursorLayer::doBeginFrame
prose: Precondition: m_backend is valid and its graphicsBufferAllocator() is usable; targetRect() gives the cursor buffer size. Postcondition: if m_swapchain is null or its size differs from targetRect().size(), m_swapchain is replaced by a new QPainterSwapchain of that size with format DRM_FORMAT_ARGB8888. It then assigns m_back = m_swapchain->acquire() (this overwrites the previous m_back even when acquire fails). If m_back is empty it returns std::nullopt and m_renderTime is left unchanged. Otherwise it stores a new CpuRenderTimeQuery in m_renderTime and returns an OutputLayerBeginFrameInfo whose renderTarget wraps m_back->view()->image() and whose repaint region is Region::infinite().
note: checked wayland_qpainter_backend.cpp:99-116. Old prose said the layer 'keeps no new buffer' on failure; actually m_back is set to the empty acquire result (line 106). Real name is the qualified member.

name: WaylandQPainterCursorLayer::doEndFrame
prose: Precondition: doBeginFrame succeeded earlier so m_renderTime and m_back are non-null; m_output refers to a WaylandOutput whose backend can import the buffer; frame may be null. Postcondition: m_renderTime->end() is called; if frame is non-null the query is moved into it via addRenderTimeQuery (if frame is null the query stays in m_renderTime); the back buffer is imported with backend()->importBuffer (asserted non-null with Q_ASSERT, a no-op in release builds); the output's cursor()->update is called with that buffer, the buffer size divided by the output scale and hotspot().toPoint(); the back buffer is released to the swapchain; the function then returns true. It has a single return statement, which returns true. renderedDeviceRegion and damagedDeviceRegion are not used.
note: checked wayland_qpainter_backend.cpp:118-130; single return at 129.

name: Rect::moveTo(int x, int y)
prose: Precondition: none beyond int arithmetic not overflowing (it is noexcept and allocates nothing). Postcondition: equivalent to moveTopLeft(QPoint(x, y)): the left edge becomes x and the top edge becomes y, and the right and bottom edges are shifted by the same offsets, so width and height are unchanged. It returns nothing and does not transfer locks, references or memory.
note: checked rect.h:1516-1519, 1492-1496 (moveTopLeft calls moveLeft/moveTop, which add the offset to the opposite edge, e.g. 1471-1476). Reviewer is right: old prose said right/bottom edges unchanged.

name: Rect::moveTo(const QPoint &point)
prose: Precondition: none beyond int arithmetic not overflowing (noexcept, no allocation). Postcondition: calls moveTopLeft(point): the left edge becomes point.x() and the top edge point.y(), and the right and bottom edges are shifted by the same offsets, so width and height are unchanged. It returns nothing and transfers no locks, references or memory.

name: RenderLoop::scheduleRepaint
prose: Precondition: d is non-null; item and outputLayer may be null. workspace(), the active window and d->output are checked before use. Postcondition: vrr is true for presentation modes AdaptiveSync/AdaptiveAsync and tearing for Async/AdaptiveAsync. If (vrr or tearing) and workspace() is non-null and has an active window and d->output is non-null, and also (item or outputLayer) is non-null, activeWindowControlsVrrRefreshRate() is true, item != the active window's surfaceItem and !surfaceItem->isAncestorOf(item), then d->delayedVrrTimer is started with 1000ms/30 and the function returns without touching the other scheduling helpers. In every other case the delayed VRR timer is stopped and then exactly one of d->scheduleNextRepaint() (when d->pendingFrameCount < effectiveMax and d->inhibitCount is zero, effectiveMax being 1 if vrr or tearing, else d->maxPendingFrameCount) or d->delayScheduleRepaint() is called. The function itself does not assign pendingFrameCount or inhibitCount, but the helpers it calls may change scheduling state.
note: checked renderloop.cpp:256-275. Old reviewer claims (pendingFrameCount never exceeds max; no modification) concerned earlier wordings; present prose says only that this function does not assign those fields, which is true by lines 256-275.

name: GlobalShortcutFilter::touchDown
prose: Precondition: event is a valid TouchDownEvent; this is the GlobalShortcutFilter member (input.cpp:1187) and its members m_gestureTaken, m_gestureCancelled, m_touchPoints, m_lastTouchDownTime and m_syntheticCancel are consistent; workspace()->outputAt(event->pos) must return a valid output when a point is already tracked. Postcondition, by exit: (1) if m_gestureTaken is true: input()->shortcuts()->processSwipeCancel(DeviceType::Touchscreen), m_gestureCancelled = true, return true; the point is not recorded. (2) Otherwise, if m_touchPoints is empty, m_lastTouchDownTime = event->time and flow continues to step 5. (3) If points are tracked and event->time - m_lastTouchDownTime > 250ms: m_gestureCancelled = true and return false, without updating m_lastTouchDownTime and without recording the point. (4) If points are tracked and the time check passes: m_lastTouchDownTime = event->time is updated first, then the distance test runs over the tracked points using the output's orientated physical size (190x100 if that size is invalid) and accepts if some tracked point has |xfactor*dx| + |yfactor*dy| < 50; if no point matches, m_gestureCancelled = true and return false (the time was already updated, the point is not recorded). (5) Otherwise m_touchPoints.insert(event->id, event->pos); if m_touchPoints.count() >= 3 and m_gestureCancelled is false, it sets m_gestureTaken = true, sets m_syntheticCancel true while input()->processFilters(&InputEventFilter::touchCancel) runs, resets it to false, calls processSwipeStart(DeviceType::Touchscreen, count) and returns true. (6) In all other cases it returns false. The event is not owned by this function.
note: checked input.cpp:1187-1229; class is GlobalShortcutFilter (starts 1037). Reviewer round 15 is right (distance mismatch path updates m_lastTouchDownTime at 1201 before returning false at 1215) and round 2 is right (returns true whenever m_gestureTaken); both are now stated.

name: EglContext::checkTimerQuerySupport
prose: Precondition: the context's m_isOpenglES flag, m_version and extension set have been set; the function is const and acquires or releases nothing. It is also called from the constructor's member-initializer list (eglcontext.cpp:116). Postcondition: returns false if the environment variable KWIN_NO_TIMER_QUERY is set (any value). Otherwise, if the context is OpenGL ES it returns true exactly when the version is at least 3.0 and GL_EXT_disjoint_timer_query is present; if it is desktop OpenGL it returns true when the version is at least 3.3 or GL_ARB_timer_query is present.

name: EglContext::checkSupported
prose: Precondition: the context's extension set, OpenGL version, m_isOpenglES flag and m_shaderManager are initialised; the function is const. Postcondition: returns false when any of the following is not supported: GLSL (ES, or the ARB shader_objects/fragment_shader/vertex_shader extensions), non-power-of-two textures (ES, or GL_ARB_texture_non_power_of_two), 3D textures (non-ES, or ES 3.0, or GL_OES_texture_3D), framebuffer objects (ES, or version 3.0, or GL_ARB_framebuffer_object or GL_EXT_framebuffer_object) and unpack-subimage (non-ES, or GL_EXT_unpack_subimage). If all are supported it asks the shader manager for the shader with traits MapTexture | TransformColorspace | AdjustSaturation | Modulate and returns shader->isValid(). Nothing is returned to the caller to own.

name: GLVertexBuffer::map<T>(size_t count)
prose: Precondition: the buffer is not currently mapped and a GL context is current. count T-sized elements are requested; the data store does not need to be large enough because the non-template map(size_t) reallocates it if it is smaller. Postcondition: calls the non-template map(sizeof(T) * count). If that returns a non-null pointer, returns a std::span<T> of count elements starting at that pointer (reinterpret_cast, no alignment check); if it returns null, returns std::nullopt. The pointer may refer to a GL-mapped range, a persistent idle range or client-side memory depending on the buffer mode (glvertexbuffer.cpp:385-410). The caller must call unmap() and must not make GL calls that access the buffer while it is mapped.
note: checked glvertexbuffer.h:176-184 and glvertexbuffer.cpp:385-410. Reviewer is right: old precondition said count elements must fit, but the doc comment and implementation reallocate.

name: OutputConfigurationStore::save
prose: Precondition: this OutputConfigurationStore holds the current m_outputs and m_setups. Postcondition: builds a JSON array with an 'outputs' object (one entry per m_outputs element, each field written only when the optional is set or the string is non-empty) and a 'setups' object (per setup the lidClosed flag and its outputs' enabled, outputIndex, priority, position and replicationSource). Then it forms the path QStandardPaths::writableLocation(ConfigLocation) + '/kwinoutputconfig.json'. If opening it for writing fails it logs a warning with qCWarning and returns without writing. Otherwise it writes document.toJson() and flushes; the QFile is closed by its destructor. It returns void and the caller acquires no lock or memory.
note: slice cut the head: the real function is OutputConfigurationStore::save at outputconfigurationstore.cpp:1301-1520 (tail only in slice 1451-1520). Two exits: early return at 1515, normal end at 1520.

name: OutputConfigurationStore::generateConfig
prose: Precondition: outputs holds valid BackendOutput pointers; m_outputs and m_setups hold the stored state; input() is available if chooseScale needs it for an internal output. Postcondition: (1) if isLidClosed is true and generateLidClosedConfig(outputs) returns a value, that configuration is returned immediately. (2) Otherwise findPartialSetup(outputs, isLidClosed) and the kscreen config (readOutputConfig) are fetched, and the outputs are reordered with std::ranges::partition so that outputs for which findOutputIndex found a stored OutputState (members of globalOutputIndices) come first; outputs with no stored state stay after them, and the order within each group is not guaranteed. (3) For each output a change set is filled: if a partial setup exists and has a state for the output's stored index, enabled, pos and priority come from that setup state, else enabled comes from the kscreen change set or defaults to true unless the lid is closed on an internal output when more than one output exists, pos is the running rightMostPosition (initially (0,0)) and priority is the running counter. mode is the output's own mode equal to the stored mode (size, refresh rate, flags if stored), else the kscreen mode, else chooseMode(output). Stored values (the m_outputs entry, empty if none) are used for scale (else chooseScale; the kscreen scale is deliberately ignored); for transform, manualTransform, overscan, rgbRange and vrrPolicy the stored value is used first, then the kscreen value, then a default; and for the other fields (HDR, reference luminance, wide gamut, auto-rotation, colour profile source, brightness, SDR software brightness, colour power tradeoff, DDC/CI flags, EDR policy, sharpness, automatic brightness) stored value else a hard-coded default; uuid, maxBitsPerColor, customModes and autoBrightnessCurve are copied from the stored state. (4) The priority counter advances and, for enabled outputs, rightMostPosition is updated to the output's top-right corner when that is further right (or same x and higher). The function returns the filled OutputConfiguration. It has two returns (lid-closed config and the final return).
note: checked outputconfigurationstore.cpp:623-725 and findOutputIndex 198-296 / findPartialSetup 582-621. Reviewer round 1 (kscreen scale ignored) right; round 2 (hardcoded defaults) right; round 15 claim that partition is a no-op is WRONG: findOutputIndex can return nullopt (lines 267, 294), so globalOutputIndices does not contain all outputs; but it does contain every output with a stored state, not only those covered by the setup, which the old prose got wrong.

name: OutputConfigurationStore::chooseScale
prose: Precondition: output and mode are valid; for an internal output input()->devices() is consulted. Postcondition: returns 1.0 if the output's physical height or width is below 3. Otherwise it picks targetDpi and minSize (internal output with a lid switch: 125 and 800; internal without: 150 and 360; external with physical height above 500: 30.5 and 800; other external: 96 and 800), computes for each axis the pixel density dpi = pixels / (physical mm / 25.4), a maximum scale clamp(pixels / minSize, 1.0, 3.0) and scale clamp(dpi / targetDpi, 1.0, thatMax), takes the smaller of the two, rounds it to the nearest multiple of 0.05 with std::round and, if the rounded result is below 1.20, returns 1.0 instead. The returned value is therefore 1.0 or a multiple of 0.05 between 1.20 and about 3.0 (rounding can exceed the per-axis maximum by up to 0.025). It has two returns (early 1.0 at line 806 and the final return at 866).
note: slice cut the head: real function is OutputConfigurationStore::chooseScale at outputconfigurationstore.cpp:801-867; slice covers only lines 849-867 of it. Old prose said the result never exceeds min(maxScaleX,maxScaleY) and that raw<1.2 gives 1.0; both imprecise (rounding precedes the 1.20 test, and rounding can overshoot).

name: EisInputCapture::handleEvents
prose: Precondition: m_eis is a valid eis context; m_client, m_seat, m_pointer, m_keyboard and m_absoluteDevice are null or valid references held by this object. Postcondition: calls eis_dispatch, then loops over eis_get_event until it returns null. Per event: CLIENT_CONNECT disconnects a sender client or a second client (leaving m_client unchanged), otherwise connects the client, sets m_client and creates m_seat configured with the allowed capabilities; CLIENT_DISCONNECT for a client other than m_client does nothing; SEAT_BIND creates or removes m_absoluteDevice, m_pointer and m_keyboard according to the capabilities bound; DEVICE_CLOSED nulls whichever of the three members equals the device, then calls eis_device_remove and eis_device_unref on it; other types are logged. After each of these the event is eis_event_unref'd. The exception is CLIENT_DISCONNECT for client == m_client: it unrefs and nulls m_seat and m_client, calls m_manager->removeInputCapture(QDBusObjectPath(m_dbusPath)) and returns from the function at line 274 without unref'ing that event and without touching m_pointer, m_keyboard or m_absoluteDevice. The loop otherwise returns when no events remain.
note: slice cut the head: real function is EisInputCapture::handleEvents at eisinputcapture.cpp:232-325. Old prose claimed device pointers are always null or valid on other paths; on the m_client disconnect return they are left as they were. Event leak on that return checked at 274 vs the unref at 323.

name: grabTexture
prose: Precondition: texture and target are valid pointers, a GL context is current (EglContext::currentContext() is used) and target has allocated storage. Postcondition: a static function. If texture->contentTransform() is Normal or FlipY it calls doGrabTexture(texture, target), which returns without writing target when texture->size() != target->size(), otherwise reads the texture pixels into target (readnpixels through a temporary framebuffer on GLES or NVIDIA, else glGetnTexImage) and flips the rows when needed. For any other transform it computes size = contentTransform.map(texture->size()); if allocating the GL_RGBA8 backing texture fails it returns with target unchanged; otherwise it renders texture into the backing texture through a framebuffer (this happens even if sizes will not match target), then calls doGrabTexture(backingTexture, target), which again leaves target untouched if the sizes differ. So target is filled only when the (transformed) texture size equals target->size(); the transformed path may still perform GL work before returning without modifying target.
note: checked screencastutils.h:42-104. Reviewer round 2 right (transformed case allocates and renders before the size check in doGrabTexture), round 15 right that a current GL context is needed; target pixel format mismatch is not checked, buffer size is passed as target->sizeInBytes().

prose: Precondition: Cursors::self() and effects are valid. Postcondition: returns immediately with no state change if the cursor is hidden (Cursors::self()->isCursorHidden()) or the mouse cursor has a source that is blank. Otherwise it creates or finds the entry m_startups[id] and sets its icon, replaces its expiredTimer with a new single-shot QTimer started with m_timeout whose timeout calls gotRemoveStartup(id), sets m_currentStartup = id and calls start(startup). start(), in turn, returns without doing anything when m_type is NoFeedback, a splash is visible, effects->isCursorHidden() is true, or no output is found at the cursor position; otherwise it connects mouseChanged only if m_active was false, sets m_active = true, and, whether or not it was already active, reads the cursor size, computes the icon size, prepares the textures, sets m_dirtyRect/m_currentGeometry to feedbackRect() and adds a repaint for that rect.
note: checked startupfeedback.cpp:271-295 and 322-354. Reviewer round 15 is right (reading size, preparing textures and repainting happen even if already active); round 2 right too (effect may already be active when start returns early); both are now in the prose.

name: KWIN_EFFECT_FACTORY_SUPPORTED(TilesEditorEffect, "metadata.json.stripped", return TilesEditorEffect::supported();)
prose: Macro invocation (effect.h:1003-1004, expanding KWIN_EFFECT_FACTORY_SUPPORTED_ENABLED at 976-998) that generates a factory class named KWIN_PLUGIN_FACTORY_NAME deriving from KWin::EffectPluginFactory with Q_PLUGIN_METADATA using "metadata.json.stripped". Generated members: empty constructor and destructor; isSupported() const returning TilesEditorEffect::supported(); enabledByDefault() const returning true; createEffect() const returning new TilesEditorEffect() unconditionally, without consulting supported().
note: old prose wrongly said the factory returns a null pointer when supported() is false (effect.h:994-997).

name: TouchPointsEffect::colorForId
prose: Precondition: any quint32 id is accepted; m_colors is valid. Postcondition: if id is already a key of m_colors, the stored Qt::GlobalColor is returned and nothing changes. Otherwise a function-local static counter s_colorIndex (shared by all instances, initially -1) is advanced by one modulo 10, s_colors[s_colorIndex] is inserted into m_colors under id and returned. The ten palette entries in order are blue, red, green, cyan, magenta, yellow, gray, darkBlue, darkRed, darkGreen, so the result is always one of them.
note: checked touchpoints.cpp:36-58. Static counter is shared across instances (line 54), first new id gets blue.
